part2.intro: Three young people talk about the things they keep from their holidays.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Lucas
texts.text: Wherever I go, I keep my tickets – bus tickets, train tickets, museum tickets, even cinema tickets. I stick them in a big book with the date and a few words about the day. My dad started doing the same thing when he was young, and he still has his books from the 1990s. My oldest ticket is from a zoo in Berlin. I was only three, so I don't remember the trip, but I love looking at it.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Thu
texts.text: I always take a diary on holiday. Every evening I write about what we did and what we ate. Sometimes I even keep the menu from a restaurant and put it in my diary! Last summer in Japan I wrote forty pages. My English teacher read some of it and asked me to write an article for the school magazine. Writing is my favourite thing, and I want to be a travel writer when I'm older.

texts.label: C
texts.title: Grace
texts.text: I buy a postcard in every town I visit, but I don't send it to my friends. I write a message to myself and post it home! When I get back from holiday, the postcards are waiting for me. It's like getting a letter from the past. Some of them never arrive – one from Greece got lost. My little brother thinks it's a crazy idea, but I've got sixty postcards now.

items.q: Who got the idea for their hobby from a parent?
Who keeps something from where they had a meal?
Who has sometimes lost one of the things they collect?
Who has something from a trip that they can't remember?
Whose holiday writing was read by a teacher?
Who says a family member doesn't understand their hobby?
Who has a plan for a future job?

part3.title: Summer at the hotel
part3.text:
Fifteen-year-old Carlos Mendes doesn't spend his summer holidays on the beach. He works at his parents' small hotel in a seaside town in Portugal. "It's hard work, but I love it," he says.

Carlos starts at eight o'clock in the morning. First, he helps his mother in the office. When new guests arrive, he asks them to fill in a form and show their passports. "I've seen passports from more than thirty countries," he says. "My favourite was from New Zealand – it had pictures of birds on the pages."

Carlos speaks English and French, so he also answers emails from people who want to book a room. "My dad's English isn't very good, so he's happy that I can help," he says. Last year Carlos also wrote a new menu for the hotel restaurant in three languages. Before that, some guests ordered fish when they really wanted chicken!

In the afternoon, Carlos is free. He usually goes swimming with his friends or reads in his room. But at eight o'clock in the evening he's back at work, giving guests their bills and answering questions about buses and boat trips.

Carlos doesn't get money for his work, but his parents pay for something special for him every year. This summer he's going to a football camp in Spain. "I've already got my ticket, and I've filled in all the forms," he smiles. "Now I just need to find my own passport!"

He asks to see their documents.

options: His dad can't speak English well.

Some guests didn't understand the old menu.

items.q: What does Carlos do in the evening?
options: He goes swimming with his friends.
He takes guests on boat trips.

items.q: How do Carlos's parents thank him for his work?
options: They give him money every week.
They have bought him a new passport.
They are paying for a trip for him.

part4.title: The history of the passport
part4.text:
People have used travel documents for hundreds of years. In the past, a passport was usually a letter from a king or queen. It asked people in other countries to {19} the traveller to pass safely through their land.

For a long time, passports didn't have photos. Instead, they {20} what the traveller looked like – for example, 'tall, with brown hair and a long nose'. Photos {21} to appear in passports about a hundred years ago.

Today, passports in almost every country look quite similar. They are small books with the traveller's name, date of birth and photo inside. Many passports also have a very small computer inside which {22} information about the person.

When you travel, you must {23} care of your passport, because it can take weeks to get a new one. Some people keep a photo of their passport on their phone, {24} case they lose it.

part7.instruction: Look at the three pictures. Write the story shown in the pictures. Write 35 words or more.

pictures.caption: a family with suitcases arriving at an airport
at the check-in desk, a boy looking in his empty bag while a woman waits for his passport
the boy's sister running towards them, holding a passport

part7.model: Last summer the Lee family went to the airport to fly to Spain. At the check-in desk, the woman asked for their passports, but Tim couldn't find his! He was very worried. Then his sister Amy came running. Tim's passport was on the seat of the car. Everyone laughed.

items.q: What has the girl forgotten to pack?

script.t: Have you got everything for the trip, Zara? Your passport?
Yes, it's in my bag with my ticket.
What about your diary? You always write in it on holiday.
Oh no, it's still on my desk! Thanks, Dad. I'll go and get it.

items.q: How much did the boy pay for his train ticket?

script.t: How much was your train ticket to London, Noah?
It's usually twenty-four pounds, but I showed my student card, so it was half price.
So only twelve pounds? That's cheap!
Yes. My friend Jack forgot his card, so he paid twenty pounds for his.

items.q: Where will the family eat tonight?

script.t: Shall we eat at the hotel tonight? I saw the menu – it looks good.
It's very expensive. What about the pizza place near the beach?
We had pizza last night. Let's try the fish restaurant by the harbour. The man at reception says it's the best in town.
OK, let's go there.

items.q: What will the boy buy for his grandmother?

script.t: I want to get something for Grandma from Edinburgh. Maybe a postcard?
You can send her a postcard, but get her a present too. What about a guidebook? She's coming here next year.
She's already got one. I'll get her this calendar with pictures of the castle. She can put it in her kitchen.

items.q: Which document does the man need to show?

script.t: Good morning. Can I see your passport, please?
Oh, I left it at the hotel. Is that a problem?
Not for hiring a car. What I really need to see is your driving licence.
Here it is. And do I pay by card now?
No, you can pay when you bring the car back.

part2.intro: You will hear a teacher talking to students about a school trip to France.
part2.title: School Trip to France

items.label: Bring this to school next week:
Give the yellow form to: Mrs

script.t: Hello, everyone. I've got some important information about our school trip to France in May. We'll leave school by coach very early on Tuesday the fourteenth. Many of you thought we were going on Monday, but that's a holiday, so it's Tuesday. Everyone must have a passport, of course. Please bring your passport to school next week, so I can make a copy of it. Don't bring your ticket – I've got all the tickets here in my office. Your parents need to fill in the yellow form and sign it. Please give the forms to Mrs Quinn, not to me. That's Q-U-I-N-N. She works in the school office. Every student also needs travel insurance. It costs fifteen pounds. Last year it was twenty, so it's a bit cheaper this time. You can pay at the office. While we're in France, you'll have to write in a diary every evening, in French, about what you did that day. It'll be part of your French project when we come back. Don't bring a laptop – an ordinary notebook is fine. OK, any questions?

part3.intro: You will hear Sara talking to her friend Tom about her holiday in Italy.

items.q: How did Sara's family travel to Italy?
What did Sara's dad lose?
Where did the family stay in Italy?
Why didn't Tom get a postcard?
options: It got lost in the post.

items.q: What did Sara enjoy most?

script.t: Hi Sara! How was Italy?
Amazing! But the start was a bit difficult.
Why? Was it the flight?
We didn't fly. The plane tickets were too expensive in August, and Dad didn't want to drive all that way. So we went by train. It took two days!
Wow. Was that the problem?
No, the train was fun. The problem was on the first night. Dad lost his wallet in the station in Paris. All his bank cards were in it.
Oh no! What about his passport and his ticket?
Luckily they were in Mum's bag. And we had travel insurance, so we got the money back later.
Where did you stay? In a hotel?
We looked at some hotels online, but my aunt lives in Florence, so we stayed in her flat. It was great.
Did you send any postcards? I didn't get one!
I wrote you one, honestly! I had your address and everything. But I forgot to post it. It's still in my bag – here you are!
Ha, thanks! So what did you enjoy most?
The food was great, and the museums were interesting, but the best thing was the boat trip to a small island. We swam all afternoon.

items.intro: You will hear a woman talking to a boy at a cinema.
items.q: Why can't the boy go in?
options: His ticket is for a different film.

script.t: Sorry, you can't go into Screen 2 with this ticket.
But I paid for it online this morning! And I'm fourteen.
Yes, but it's a ticket for Screen 3 – the film about the space ship. This is Screen 2. It's a different film.
Oh! I'm so sorry.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking to her brother about a form.
items.q: What is the form for?

script.t: Can you help me with this form? It asks for my date of birth, my address and the name of my school.
What's it for? The swimming club?
No, that's next month. It's for the library. When I've got a card, I can borrow ten books at a time.

items.intro: You will hear a man talking about his job.
items.q: What is his job?
options: He works in a travel agency.

script.t: I start work very early, at six o'clock. First I collect the letters, cards and magazines at the office, and then I walk round the town with them. I read the newspaper on my break! Lots of people say hello to me. The worst thing is the dogs – some of them don't like me at all!

items.intro: You will hear a girl leaving a message for her friend.
items.q: Why is she calling?
options: to invite her friend to a party
to thank her friend for a present

script.t: Hi Jade, it's Sofia. I just got your card in the post. It's beautiful! And thank you so much for the book. I started reading it last night and I can't stop. You know me so well! I'll tell you all about my party at school tomorrow. Bye!

items.intro: You will hear a boy talking to his father about a newspaper.
items.q: How does the boy feel?

script.t: Dad, have you seen today's newspaper? Look at page six!
Is that your football team?
Yes! There's a photo of us, and they wrote about my goal! I've never been in a newspaper before. I'm going to buy five copies – one for Grandma, one for Uncle Kai…
That's wonderful!

part5.intro: You will hear Ethan talking to his mum before a family holiday. Where is each thing now?

script.t: Mum, have you got my passport? I can't find it.
Don't worry. I've got all the passports in my handbag. I don't want anyone to lose them.
OK. What about the train tickets? Are they in the blue bag?
No. I printed them this morning, but I forgot to take them off the printer. They're still there. Can you get them later?
Sure. And the insurance papers? Dad said they were in the kitchen drawer.
They were, but I've put them in the blue bag now, with the hotel information.
Good. I'm going to take my diary. It's on my desk. Shall I put it in my backpack?
Your backpack's already very full. Put it in the suitcase. There's space at the top.
OK, there – I've just put it in the suitcase. Oh, and Dad's looking for his driving licence. He needs it to hire a car in Spain. He thinks he left it in the car.
Tell him to look in his jacket. He always keeps it there, in the inside pocket.
Dad's just looked – you're right, it's in his jacket! I think we're nearly ready!
